# dtcloud_snapshots (Data Source)

Lists every snapshot visible to the caller.

Not a duplicate of `dtcloud_volume_snapshots`, which reads a different endpoint scoped to one volume
and sorted newest first. This one covers every snapshot, in the platform's own order.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_snapshots" "ready" {
  status = "available"
}

data "dtcloud_snapshots" "of_data_volume" {
  volume_id = dtcloud_volume.data.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name` (String) Only return snapshots with this exact name. Applied by the provider.
- `status` (String) Only return snapshots in this status, e.g. `available`. Applied by the provider.
- `volume_id` (String) Only return snapshots of this volume. Applied by the provider.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `snapshots` (List of Object) The snapshots that matched, in the order the platform returned them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--snapshots))

<a id="nestedatt--snapshots"></a>
### Nested Schema for `snapshots`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String)
- `description` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `size` (Number)
- `status` (String)
- `storage_policy` (String)
- `updated_at` (String)
- `volume_id` (String)
- `volume_type_id` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **The filters are applied by the provider**, since the list endpoint takes none, and they combine.
  `volume_id` and `name` match exactly and `status` ignores case. A filter that matches nothing returns
  an empty list.
* **`storage_policy` is resolved once per run** from `volume_type_id`, and is empty if that lookup
  fails.
* **There is no `progress` or `project_id` here.** The list endpoint does not report them; read one
  snapshot with `dtcloud_snapshot` when you need either.
